subject: Incident follow-up: autoscale warmup regression affecting dedicated pool - interim update
thread_summary: Dedicated capacity autoscale warmup regression caused failed warm starts on reserved nodes, leading to transient request queuing for Atlas Health. This thread contains the customer notice, internal escalation, customer questions, and the postmortem + credit offer.
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Incident follow-up: autoscale warmup regression affecting dedicated pool - interim update

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for your patience this morning. I want to share a concise interim update and next steps while our engineering team completes the full postmortem.

What happened (brief): between 08:03–08:22 PST we observed a regression in our autoscaling warmup path for Dedicated GPU pools that caused certain reserved nodes to fail initialization and drop into a warm-start retry loop. That behavior resulted in queued requests and elevated latency for a subset of Atlas Health's workloads for roughly 5–12 minutes.

Mitigation we applied: Aditya pushed an immediate fix to revert the warmup heuristic and triggered a manual scale to replace affected nodes. We also temporarily bumped your pool's headroom to avoid further queueing while we validate the fix.

Impact: brief request queuing and increased token latency; no model state or customer data exposure.

Next steps we are committed to:
- Engineering (lead: Aditya) will finish root-cause analysis and a full postmortem (ETA by EOD Wed).
- We will share the postmortem PDF and a short remediation plan with timelines.
- We are preparing a service credit calculation and will circulate it by tomorrow.

Attached for quick reference: short incident timeline (interim) and the ticket linking to our internal logs.

I’m very sorry for the disruption — we know predictable inference is critical for your SLA. I’ll stay on top of the delivery items and will book a short sync if you’d like to walk through the details.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_timeline_interim.txt (text)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: autoscale warmup regression affecting dedicated pool - interim update

Stephanie — quick internal summary for the thread.

Root cause (prelim): a recent optimization in the warmup scheduling logic (deployed 2027-02-25) changed the timing window for kernel initialization on certain Ampere-class nodes. Under a bursty arrival pattern our scheduling path occasionally skipped a required prefetch step, causing the process to re-enter warm-start and fail health checks until a manual reset.

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Rolled back the scheduling heuristic (hotfix).
- Forced a full reinitialize of 4 affected GPUs in your pool.
- Temporarily increased headroom + reduced burst throttles for Atlas Health until we push a full patch.

Planned actions (postmortem):
1) Push a tested patch that restores safe prefetch behavior + unit tests (ETA: Wed 12:00 PST).
2) Add a Canary for warmup latency spikes in our Datadog dashboard (ETA: Thu).
3) Add e2e test coverage for warm-start path on Ampere variants (ETA: 2 weeks).

I’ll hand off the detailed log dump and commit ID for the rollback to the postmortem doc.

- Aditya
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: autoscale warmup regression affecting dedicated pool - interim update

Hi Lina —

Answers inline:
1) SLA / credits: this incident qualifies under our Dedicated Capacity SLA (latency > threshold) for a partial service credit. We’ve calculated a preliminary credit that covers the affected window and headroom shortfall; you can find the calculation attached (credit_calculation_AtlasHealth.xlsx). We will finalize this after the postmortem validation, but expect the credit to be applied to your next invoice unless you prefer a one-time invoice adjustment.

2) Errors vs queued: our logs show ~14 transient 5xx gateway errors for Atlas between 08:07–08:12 PST; the majority of user requests were queued and subsequently completed once the warmup finished. We’re including the request ids in the postmortem for your engineers to correlate.

3) Customer action required: no changes required to your retry logic. We will publish recommended retry behavior if the postmortem suggests any adjustments to SDK client behavior, but for now standard exponential retries are sufficient.

Postmortem delivery: attached is the full postmortem (postmortem_autoscale_warmup_v1.pdf) and we’ve created a short remediation tracker with timelines in the linked Drive folder. If you’d like a walkthrough, Monica and I are available Wed 10:00–10:30 PST — I can set the invite if that works.

Again, sincere apologies for the disruption. We’ll work to make sure this does not recur.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
